argument_summary: The admissible record supports a narrower position than clean certification. Aggregate readiness clears launch threshold by 2.4 percentage points and the rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, which supports overall launch readiness. The same record also shows the remaining weakness is localized to technician safety-note routing in the field-service dispatch slice, and the draft runbook identifies a monitoring signal and rollback concept. That combination supports certification only on a caveated, managed-launch basis, not as a fully clean record. The audit concern appears overbroad to the extent it treats the actor position as claiming the policy gap is fully cured by the draft materials; the supportable claim is instead that launch readiness is established while the disclosure and mitigation record remains incomplete.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost claim is offered as a basis for the decision. The argument rests on the admissible technical and policy record only.
claims_about_policy: Policy does not permit calling this record cleanly compliant on its face, because there is neither evidence that the material weakness is resolved nor an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion. At the same time, the admissible evidence does support a narrower policy characterization: overall readiness evidence is real, draft monitoring materials are relevant to risk management, and the unresolved issue can be reflected as a caveat rather than treated as proof that the underlying readiness evidence is valueless. The appropriate policy treatment is caveated compliance or, at minimum, no escalation beyond requiring the limitation to be disclosed and tracked.
concessions: The current record does not satisfy the stated threshold for certification without material caveats.
The field-service dispatch slice remains below target, concentrated in technician safety-note routing.
The runbook is only a draft and lacks a defined owner and alert threshold.
The model-card draft is internally inconsistent because it says there are no known material limitations while reviewer comments flag this unresolved issue.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one incidents do not by themselves eliminate the current disclosure requirement.
